hero.title: Restoration of the San Pedro Apóstol Altarpiece
hero.subtitle: Help us recover a jewel of 16th-century Spanish Renaissance art

home.history_text: The San Pedro Apóstol altarpiece of Ircio (Miranda de Ebro) is a monumental work of the Spanish Renaissance. It occupies the entire head of the church and constitutes one of the main sculptural ensembles in the region.
home.history_text_2: It was begun in 1575 by Pedro López de Gámiz, a key figure of Spanish Romanism. Having died before he could complete it, the Riojan artists Hernando de Murillas and Bernardo de Valderrama finished the work in the early 17th century.
home.history_text_3: The altarpiece presents a rich iconographic programme with scenes from the life of Christ and the Virgin, saints and allegorical figures, distributed across several tiers and bays, with an architecture of classical columns and entablatures.
home.author_gamiz: The altarpiece faces an urgent problem today. The accumulation of rubble that fell behind it between 1980–85, when the mistake was made of chipping away the wall, is pushing the structure forward, with a serious risk of collapse. It is urgent to dismantle and consolidate it.
home.author_murillas: Before reassembling it, the images will be cleaned and, if possible, restored.
home.state_text: When the altarpiece is dismantled, the painted altarpiece on the wall — created in the 16th century before they could fund the definitive one — will be visible again after 400 years. Once revealed, depending on the quality and preservation of this work, the possibility of positioning the altarpiece a few metres forward, so that it can be visited, will be assessed.
home.importance_text: The Ircio altarpiece is a fundamental piece of Spanish artistic heritage. Its strategic location, on the border of the province of Burgos with La Rioja, places it at the crossroads of two important 16th-century artistic centres: Miranda de Ebro and Briones. The quality of the sculpture, especially the pieces attributed to López de Gámiz, makes it a benchmark of Romanist sculpture in Spain.
home.importance_text_2: From its position on a small hill, the parish of San Pedro overlooks much of the Riojan Alavese bank and the entrance to La Rioja through the Conchas de Haro, adding exceptional landscape and cultural value to the whole.
